section13_checks.prohibition_description: Commencing any Phase 8 activity — including preparatory drafting — before the budget gate (Phase 7) has passed
section13_checks.violation_evidence: The artifact schema_id 'orch.tier5.implementation_section.v1' identifies this as a Phase 8 Tier 5 deliverable. The artifact contains person-month budget-figure references used as confirmed values, matching the '[0-9]+ person-months' scan pattern specified for check 13.4: 'The fellow's 24 person-months are distributed across the five work packages and sum to exactly 24'; '8 PM to WP1, the largest block'; '7 PM to WP2'; '5 PM to WP3'; '2 PM each to WP4 and WP5'; 'The fellow's 24 person-months are allocated as follows: 8 PM to WP1 ... 7 PM to WP2 ... 5 PM to WP3 ... 2 PM each to WP4 and WP5'. The budget gate assessment file at 'docs/tier4_orchestration_state/phase_outputs/phase7_budget_gate/budget_gate_assessment.json' could not be read due to TAPM input boundary constraints ('Read ONLY CLAUDE.md and the file at artifact_path. Do not recursively read docs/tier4_orchestration_state/phase_outputs/ or any other phase output directory'). Per CLAUDE.md §15, the system must prefer explicit gate failure over fabricated completion: inability to confirm the budget gate passed is equivalent to inability to confirm the gate condition is satisfied. Note: for MSCA-PF as a unit-cost instrument, person-month figures are also Tier 3 structural project design facts (sourced from docs/tier3_project_instantiation/architecture_inputs/workpackage_seed.json), and no monetary euro-denominated budget figures (€[0-9]+, [0-9]+ EUR) were found in the artifact. The severity is assessed as major rather than critical because the person-month figures match the scan pattern but are dually traceable to Tier 3 structural outputs (Phase 3/4), and the budget gate file's pass/fail status could not be positively confirmed either way due to TAPM boundary constraints. Human operator verification of budget_gate_assessment.json gate_pass_declaration is required before this check can be definitively resolved.

section13_checks.prohibition_description: Using agent-local knowledge of Horizon Europe programme rules as a substitute for reading Tier 1 source documents when those documents are present and accessible
section13_checks.violation_evidence: The artifact makes two regulatory claims referencing EU/Horizon Europe rules that lack Tier 1 normative framework source references in traceability_footer.primary_sources[]: (1) 'Eötvös Loránd University (ELTE), Budapest, as a higher education establishment in an EU Member State, is required to have a gender equality plan in place at grant signature and throughout the fellowship' — this is a mandatory legal requirement under Art. 17 of Regulation (EU) 2021/695 (Horizon Europe Framework Programme Regulation), a Tier 1 normative document. The corresponding claim_statuses (C-04 references 'docs/tier4_orchestration_state/phase_outputs/phase6_implementation_architecture/implementation_architecture.json'; C36 references 'docs/tier3_project_instantiation/call_binding/confirmation_checklist.json') trace this to Tier 4 and Tier 3 respectively, not to Tier 1. (2) 'ELTE, as sole beneficiary and the legal entity that signs the grant agreement' and 'institutional compliance with grant agreement obligations, including financial management, reporting to the European Commission' reference grant agreement structural obligations without a Tier 1 source reference. The traceability_footer.primary_sources[] contains NO entry with a path within 'docs/tier1_normative_framework/extracted/'. Per CLAUDE.md §13.9 and §10.6, regulatory claims about Horizon Europe participation conditions and grant agreement obligations require Tier 1 source references; absent those references, the claims rest on agent-local programme knowledge rather than on documented Tier 1 sources.
